headline: Senate rejected a resolution that would have ended the national energy emergency the President declared on January 20, 2025.
what_it_does: This resolution would have ended the national emergency on energy declared in Executive Order 14156. That order says U.S. energy supply and infrastructure are not enough to meet the country's needs. It directs federal agencies to use emergency powers to speed up approval of domestic energy projects and use emergency permitting under certain environmental rules. Ending the emergency would have removed the basis for those emergency actions, including emergency military construction tied to a Defense Department review of energy supply.

who_it_affects.how: They would have lost access to faster, emergency-based approvals and permitting for projects involving oil, gas, coal, uranium, biofuels, hydropower, geothermal, and critical minerals.
Agencies would no longer have been directed to use emergency authorities to speed up energy development and infrastructure.
It would have lost the emergency military construction authority the order invoked to address energy supply weaknesses it identified.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of the Northeast, West Coast, and Alaska
who_it_affects.how: Energy infrastructure projects the order singled out for faster completion in these regions would no longer have been sped up under emergency powers.
